rule: X-DEVLEDGER — every departure from a blueprint's literal text lives here as a first-class committed entry {blueprintLine, whatWasDone, why, lawAuthority}, surfaced verbatim in the handoff. A silent deviation is a Halt.

deviations.blueprintLine: Honesty-Layer Phase 1: 'remove the RWA verdict pin machinery'
deviations.whatWasDone: The dead RWA runtime (execRwa, the drift classifier, 11 fee-yield .py) was removed, but the wall-guarded RWA verdict PIN (RWA_VERDICT_SHA / RWA_VERDICT_INVARIANTS) was RETAINED.
deviations.why: The pin is a live integrity anchor (repro_contracts / F-ENV), not dead code. Ripping out a live wall to satisfy a cleanup parenthetical is the very 'edit the integrity machinery to help' that the record forbids — the dead runtime was removed, the wall-guarded pin stays.

deviations.whatWasDone: The front-end is server-rendered Hono HTML with minimal inline JS (no Vite / SPA / bundler).
deviations.why: PART CLEAN's stated primacy — no heavy dependency; the cheapest correct thing a stranger can run AND read. A Vite/SPA build is a heavy dependency the two-screen tool does not need.

deviations.whatWasDone: GeckoTerminal is RESOLVED — wired this sprint as the keyless third provider feeding the liquidity-depth axis.
deviations.why: The Deepening sprint's X-COVER closes the one unwired provider; the ledger records the closure so a reader sees the park was resolved, not silently dropped.

deviations.blueprintLine: Deepening Phase 3: 'the pinned DeFiLlama unlocks pull, now scored' (assumed keyless)
deviations.whatWasDone: DISCOVERED mid-sprint: DeFiLlama's unlocks/emissions endpoints (api.llama.fi/emissions, /emission/{protocol}) now return HTTP 402 'Upgrade to the paid API plan' — no longer keyless. The unlock-overhang axis is BUILT + positive-controlled (the pure nextUnlockFraction extractor + the pinned thresholds), and the client probe degrades to SAMPLE on 402, but on live keyless data with no schedule resolvable the axis renders not-applicable / UNVERIFIED — NEVER scraped, NEVER faked. The axis is ARMED for a keyless schedule source (e.g. the deferred on-chain vesting path via Alchemy/The Graph).
deviations.why: The firewall forbids faking an axis or citing a number with no honest source. A real-world data source going keyless→paid mid-sprint is surfaced as an honest UNVERIFIED, not papered over with a scrape or a fabricated fraction (X-HONEST / A'#5 — an axis that cannot be made trustworthy is a NAMED gap, never tuned to look right).

deviations.blueprintLine: Crown-Jewel Phase 2: 'UNLOCK-LIVE (X-UNLOCK-LIVE, D4): V-LIVE keyless; wire or signed cut (D6)'
deviations.whatWasDone: TAKEN — the Operator-signed SCOPE-CUT. The keyless unlock source stays unavailable: DeFiLlama's emissions feed is paywalled (probed live: api.llama.fi/emission/{protocol} and /emissions → HTTP 402 'Upgrade to the paid API plan'; coins.llama.fi/emissions → 400), and on-chain vesting (an RPC + per-token ABIs) and published-schedule scraping are both out of the keyless zero-setup mass-tool scope (the latter refused outright by the firewall). The unlock-overhang axis stays BUILT + positive-controlled + ARMED for a keyless schedule source; on live keyless data it renders not-applicable/UNVERIFIED, NEVER scraped/faked. The paywall is EVIDENCED, not asserted: data/honesty/evidence/vlive-unlock-probe.json records the live 402 probe and is covered by the capture-manifest (verify recomputes its content-hash).
deviations.why: The blueprint's X-UNLOCK-LIVE explicitly sanctions a signed scope-cut (D6) over a fabricated/scraped fetch when no honest keyless live path exists. The keyless firewall + the paywall leave no honest live path this sprint, so the cut is the honest resolution — the axis is armed for the day a keyless source returns, and the cut is surfaced verbatim, never silent.

deviations.blueprintLine: Crown-Jewel Phase 3: 'DEPENDENCY-TRUE (X-DEP, D5): score dependency; counterparty whole'
deviations.whatWasDone: RESOLVED — dependency is SCORED, no longer a non-scoring note. The counterparty screen's third signal (depProtocols = the # of distinct protocols the strategy's yield depends on) folds into the tier: a single, transparent dependency (dep ≤ 1, CP_DEP_SINGLE) is the clean direct-deposit baseline (never a flag); a STACKED strategy (dep ≥ 3, CP_DEP_STACKED) adds hidden counterparty/attack surface → a hard flag (a stacked dependency withholds a clean pass; a stacked + young/dust → fail). Derived deterministically (feed defaults a direct DeFiLlama pool to dep=1; a registry entry may declare a stacked dependency). The screen restates its inputs as age · size · dependency, and STILL never over-claims 'audited/safe/guaranteed' (the deep Sentinel IR stays PARKED).
deviations.why: The validation report's F3 (dependency demoted, not laddered) is closed: the pinned dependency signal is now scored, defaulting to the clean baseline so no existing pool's verdict moves, and only biting when a strategy genuinely stacks protocol surface.

deviations.blueprintLine: Crown-Jewel validation report V3: 'the dep=1 default is a derived modeling assumption, not laddered'
deviations.whatWasDone: LADDERED as a pinned modeling assumption: a direct DeFiLlama single-protocol pool defaults to depProtocols=1 (a single, transparent counterparty dependency — the clean baseline, never a flag). The feed sets this default (feed.ts poolFacts: depProtocols = ref.depProtocols ?? 1); a shelf-registry entry MAY declare a higher (stacked) dependency, and only then does the counterparty screen's dependency signal bite. The default only ever biases toward the transparent case, so no existing pool's verdict moves.
deviations.why: A raw DeFiLlama pool IS one protocol's deposit — one counterparty surface. Defaulting to 1 is the honest, conservative baseline (it never fabricates a stacked flag). V3 asked for the derived default to be laddered rather than left implicit: it is now recorded + evidenced here, hash-locked in persistence-pins.json (deviationD8), and surfaced verbatim in the handoff — not silent.
deviations.lawAuthority: X-DEP + X-DEVLEDGER (Crown-Jewel report V3, Persistence Phase 1)
